fields.description:
# S6 — Bounded concurrent gate executions, with fast-fail admission

Implements decision **5** of the LANDED `docs/adr/0112-on-box-disk-ceiling-architecture.md` on
`origin/main`, which enumerates SEVEN decisions; the draft quoted on prerequisite 7dfa had only
three, so every "decision N" here is checkable against the merged file, not that draft.

## Why

S2–S5 cap each accumulator via a high-water-mark GC, and **a watermark GC assumes evictable data
exists**. The janitor relies on POSIX delete-on-last-close and takes no per-reader lease, so it
may `unlink` an in-flight snapshot but the blocks are not returned until the last reader closes.
Under the operator's **~10 parallel plan reviews** the held bytes are LIVE, not garbage: the GC
finds nothing evictable and the volume fills anyway. Bounded concurrency is a **precondition**
for S2–S5. Both gates copy the repo at a ref, so they share **ONE counter** (two caps of N each
admit 2N), and at capacity the call **fast-fails**: a queued gate holds its thread and ~739 MB
resident, and holds the MCP client's request past its ~60 s deadline.

## Design

**Seam.** `peak_rss.gate_peak_rss` already wraps this scope and says why: wrapping
`review_plan()` / `verify_completion()` "covers both call paths at one seam, since both reach
the gate through these functions". Admission is its sibling, `gate_admission.gate_admission`,
entered **before** `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` in both — materialization spends the bytes.
It adds a second term to the existing pre-clone admission point (`ensure_min_free_space` /
`SnapshotLowDiskError`), not a parallel mechanism.

**Counter.** N slot files in the snapshot store's existing `locks/` dir, each held for the run
under a non-blocking `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, released in a `finally`. Cross-process
(AC4) and crash-safe (AC5: the kernel drops a flock when the holder dies — no heartbeat, which
the janitor rejected as unsound). It serialises across threads of one process too, since a flock
is held by the open file description and each acquisition opens its own; and it inherits
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, following gate scratch onto the ADR's dedicated volume.

**Fail-open, but ANNOUNCED.** If admission's own plumbing is unusable (no `fcntl` on Windows, an
unwritable store) the gate is ADMITTED: refusing would turn one unwritable directory into a
total gate outage on the host, while admitting only overshoots concurrency, with the free-space
floor and janitor still applying — the posture `has_min_free_space` already takes on `OSError`.
But a silently disarmed cap is how bug 3276 recurs, so each such admission emits one
`GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED {json}` marker naming the reason.

**Refusal — the hierarchy decides the mapping.** `GateCongestedError` lives in
`src/rebar/llm/errors.py` as a **direct subclass of `LLMError`** (not `LLMRunnerError`: no runner
ran), and its `__init__` attaches
`.outcome = LLMOutcome(ResolutionClass.WAIT_AND_RETRY, diagnostic, retryable=True)`. Those two
facts fire the mapping through arms that ALREADY exist, so **no new `except` clause is added**:

- MCP: `_review_plan_body` / `_verify_completion_body` catch `rebar.llm.LLMError` →
  `_structured_llm_failure`, which reads `outcome_of(exc)` (`getattr(exc, "outcome", None)`):
  with the outcome that gives `retryable: true` + `resolution_class: "WAIT_AND_RETRY"`, without
  it `false`. No `verdict` key, so congestion is unreadable as INDETERMINATE, BLOCK or FAIL.
- CLI: both handlers catch `llm.LLMError` → `_llm_error_exit_code`, which returns **11**
  ("transient — retry") exactly when `outcome.retryable`, else 1; an `Error:` line naming host
  congestion goes to stderr first.
- Vocabulary: `_errors._llm_error_code` gains an `isinstance(exc, GateCongestedError)` branch
  returning a new `"gate_congested"` code registered in `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`, placed **before
  every existing arm** (the bare `isinstance(exc, LLMError)` would otherwise report the refusal
  as `command_failed`). Since the error-taxonomy contract test asserts the `LLMError` family is
  EXHAUSTIVELY mapped, the subclass is registered there too — that test verifies this derivation
  in-session.

On the review-bot path this is ADR 0069's retryable-deferral shape, never an `LLM-Review −1`.

**Metric (AC7).** One line-start `GATE_CONGESTED {json}` stderr marker per refusal, copying the
`GATE_PEAK_RSS` / `VOTER_ERROR` convention: the containers hold no AWS credentials, so the host
probe greps journald. It is also portable (`project.portability`) — identical under the CLI on a
laptop with no CloudWatch and no CI provider.

**Config (AC6).** `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, resolved by `resolve_gate_max_concurrent`
beside `resolve_gate_min_free_bytes`. `0` disables the bound (the `max_bytes` idiom); a
malformed or negative value falls back to the default rather than disarming the cap. No
`REBAR_GATE_*` env tier, deviating from ADR decision 6: a new `REBAR_*` literal is a new
`env_var` mechanism and bug `a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a` makes any new mechanism unlandable today,
while `[snapshot]` keys are exempt (a `_RESERVED_SECTIONS` member, absent from `_SECTIONS`).
One line to add once `a1f1` is fixed; fuller reasoning in the design comment here.

**Default = 4, from measurement.** `GATE_PEAK_RSS`: plan_review ~748 MB, verify_completion
~462 MB (the ADR cites ~739 MB / ~4.7 min and a degraded run at 501 MB, so it varies run to
run). The host is a `t4g.large` (8 GiB) shared with Gerrit and ADR decision 7 forbids growing
it; ~2.17 GB steady state plus Gerrit's ~3 GiB config reservation leave roughly 3 GiB for gate
work. 4 × 748 MB ≈ 2.99 GB fits; a fifth run (~3.74 GB) does not. 4 is also well below the
observed ~10 concurrent — a cap at or above observed peak sheds no load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: one counter bounds both gates. Hold `limit` slots as `plan_review`, assert a
  `verify_completion` admission is refused.
- [ ] AC2: at capacity the call fast-fails — the refused call returns in under one second while
  a holder is still running.
- [ ] AC3a: the refusal names host congestion and says to retry (both words in the message).
- [ ] AC3b: it is not readable as a verdict — the MCP body returns `retryable: true`,
  `error == "gate_congested"`, and NO `verdict` key.
- [ ] AC3c: the CLI returns exit 11 for a congestion refusal.
- [ ] AC4: the bound spans processes — a real child holds every slot; this one is refused.
- [ ] AC5a: a killed holder frees its slot. SIGKILL a holder, assert a later admission succeeds.
- [ ] AC5b: a gate that raises frees its slot. Raise inside the wrapper, assert the next
  admission succeeds.
- [ ] AC6a: the cap reads `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates`, defaults to 4, treats 0 as off, and
  falls back to the default on a malformed or negative value — one test per behaviour.
- [ ] AC6b: `docs/config.md` AND `docs/plan-review-gate.md` both name the key, its default and
  its rationale, and the latter states a congestion refusal is an expected outcome, not a
  gate failure.
- [ ] AC7: a rejected admission emits exactly one `GATE_CONGESTED` marker naming gate, ticket
  and limit; an admitted one emits none.
- [ ] AC8: a disarmed cap is announced. With admission's store made unusable the gate is
  admitted AND exactly one `GATE_ADMISSION_DISARMED` marker naming the reason is emitted.

## Testing

`pytest tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py
tests/interfaces/contracts/test_error_code_taxonomy_contract.py -q`, then `make lint`,
`make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q` (not run by `make lint`;
it is what catches a new mechanism name).

## File impact

New: `llm/gate_admission.py`, `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py`. Edited: `llm/errors.py`,
`llm/plan_review/__init__.py`, `llm/completion.py`, `_config_resolvers.py`, `_errors.py`, the
error-taxonomy contract test, `docs/config.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. UNCHANGED by design:
`_mcp_llm.py`, `_cli/_llm_commands.py`.
